answer: Dwell-Weighted Witness Quota.** Each identity must accrue a rising quota of witnessed, time-stamped interactions with distinct peers before its actions carry weight, and quota decays as a tide: unused credibility recedes hourly. Because peers can only witness so many sessions, saturated attention limits how many identities an attacker can keep simultaneously credible. The cost is sustained human attention across many accounts, and a single echo of a flagged pattern resets the quota. Operators pay in labor, not tokens; saffron marks accounts whose witness graph clusters too densely.
